paper_metadata.title: Improvement of high temperature strength of 2219 alloy by Sc and Zr addition through a novel three-stage heat treatment route

evidence.quote: 2xxx series Al alloys are widely used in aviation industry for structural applications. Among them, 2219 Al alloy is one of the most important alloy for high temperature usage up to 150 ℃.
The 2219ScZr alloy was produced by the addition of equal atom percent (0.15 at%) of Sc and Zr to the commercial 2219 alloy
The 2219ScZr alloy was produced by the addition of equal atom percent (0.15 at%) of Sc and Zr to the commercial 2219 alloy
The current alloy is a commercial 2219 Al alloy with small addition of Sc and Zr designated as 2219ScZr.

Melting was carried out in a vacuum arc melting furnace under argon atmosphere. The process of melting and solidification was repeated several times to ensure proper mixing and achieving compositional homogeneity.

Subsequently, the alloy was suction cast in a water-cooled copper mould in the form of plates of dimension of 3 mm*10 mm*70 mm. A higher cooling rate between 10 2 to 10 3 K/s could be achieved during the suction casting [20].
The cast strips were subjected to direct ageing at 375 °C to allow the precipitation of Al3Sc, Al3Zr or Al3(Sc,Zr) phase.

Following this, the samples were solution treated at 535 °C for 30 min in order to increase the Cu concentration in the solid solution without significantly affecting the already formed Al3Sc, Al3Zr or Al3(Sc,Zr) precipitates.
The solution-treated samples were finally subjected to ageing at 200 °C to obtain θ′ or θ″ precipitates in the matrix [19].
Additionally, a few nanometre-sized, faceted L12 Al3Sc precipitates were observed during TEM examination.
The Cu concentration in the matrix was found to be 1.4 wt% while the composition of the grain boundary phase corresponded to intermetallic Al2Cu (θ) phase.
The optical micrograph exhibits presence of fine equiaxed grains. The average grain size is measured from EBSD micrograph and is found to be 13 ± 8 µm.

Elemental mapping of the precipitates acquired using STEM-EDS detector is shown in Fig. 4(d) that revealed the precipitates to be Al3(Sc,Zr). The average size (average of ~200 particles) is found to be 1.2 ± 0.3 nm (radius).
The average size of Al3(Sc,Zr) precipitates after solution treatment increases to 2.4 ± 1.6 nm (radius) and precipitate number density per unit volume decreases to 3.53 × 10−5 nm−3

evidence.quote: On the other hand the lengths of the θ′ precipitates are larger than 35 nm and thickness of the plate also varies between 1 nm and 5 nm.
Size of the Al3(Sc,Zr) is also measured after the second stage of ageing and average radius of the precipitates is determined as 2.4 ± 0.5 nm and number density as 3.71 × 10−5 nm−3.
The cast alloy exhibits a Vicker's hardness of 953 ± 44 MPa.
The hardness increases continuously up to 40 h with a peak hardness of 1270 ± 26 MPa following which it slightly decreases.
Consequently, hardness value decreases to 1187 ± 29 MPa.
The alloy reaches a peak hardness value of 1425 ± 29 MPa at 10 h after which it decreases to a value of 1367 ± 18 MPa after 20 h.

Presence of Al3(Sc, Zr) precipitates together with high number density of θ′′ and θ′ precipitates results in remarkably high 0.2% proof stress of 456 MPa at room temperature, 295 MPa at 200 °C and 227 MPa at 250 °C along with 5% ductility.

It is observed that both the plates are heterogeneously nucleated on pre-existing spherical Al3(Sc,Zr) precipitates.

It is reported that the heterogeneous nucleation of θ′′ and θ′ precipitates on Al3Zr precipitates slows down the coarsening kinetics of these precipitates compared to the plates obtained through homogeneous nucleation in the binary Al-Cu alloy [18].
From the preceding analysis, it is evident that the significant improvement in strength is due to the formation of θ′′, θ′ and Al3(Sc,Zr) precipitates.
Thus, the role of Al3Sc or Al3(Sc,Zr) precipitates in refining the grain size is minor, the major role being played by the high cooling rate provided by suction casting in water cooled copper moulds.
